blocks.text:
After breakfast, drive north out of Quito, past the Mitad del Mundo complex and the Equator. The road then turns west towards the Pacific side of the Andes.

Your first stop is a viewpoint by the extinct Pululahua volcano. Continue to the Tulipe Archaeological Museum, about two hours away. There you will learn about the Yumbo culture and see ancient pools and other surviving structures.

About 1.5 hours later, you will reach the entrance to the Mashpi Reserve, which covers around 1,300 hectares. Here, highland scenery gives way to humid cloud forest with rich vegetation.

Expect to arrive at the lodge between 12:00 and 12:30. After a welcome drink and check-in, there is a short orientation and time to relax before lunch.

Nature activities begin in the afternoon. The activity will be chosen according to the weather, trail conditions, group size and guests’ fitness. An evening walk may be available after dinner if conditions permit.

Wayra Rooms are about 34 m². The lodge has 19 of these rooms, 15 with double beds. Connecting rooms are available for families or friends. Rooms come with a wardrobe, safe, bathroom, hairdryer, table, chairs, furnishings, bathrobes and slippers.

**Accommodation:** Mashpi Lodge, Wayra Room.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Honour guards in blue uniforms by wooden doors in Quito, Ecuador

Spend the whole day in the reserve. If you would like to see the forest at dawn, early activities may be available before breakfast. Birds are often especially active and easy to spot at this time.

The main excursion follows breakfast. Then there is lunch and a short break. Activities resume in the afternoon, with time in between to relax at the lodge and watch the forest.

Optional night walks may be available after dinner, depending on conditions. The forest feels different after dark. The sounds change, and different animals and insects become active.

**Accommodation:** Mashpi Lodge, Wayra Room.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch and dinner.
